public_sources.bound_semantics: Flink watermarks carry event-time progress; Watermark(t) means events with timestamps <= t should have arrived, and watermarks are used to reason about out-of-order streams.
Elements arriving with timestamps <= an already-passed watermark are late elements; real systems may still observe arbitrarily delayed elements.
Beam's manual watermark estimator rejects watermark regression and requires monotonically increasing watermark values.

chat_native_reduction.watermark_policy: The controller deliberately treats event_time <= durable credit_watermark as finalized for credit, even though public stream systems may choose different late-data handling policies.
chat_native_reduction.authority_rule: Late/finalized outcomes are archive diagnostics only and cannot reopen credit or mutate current authority.
chat_native_reduction.advance_rule: The role-local credit watermark advances only after terminal evidence for the covered epoch has been durably read back.

trace_results.effect: late/finalized; archive only; no credit or authority mutation
on-time and independently evaluable; no automatic credit

credit_rule: At most one role-local credit after exact terminal readback; this file creation alone earns zero credit.
scope_limit: Fixed role-local watermark trace only. This does not claim stream watermarks are infallible completeness proofs, nor does it claim Flink/Beam themselves are accepted zero-quota runtimes.
